29.0.0.en: This feast was the first of the feasts of the seventh month and came on its first day, that is, it was the first day or head of the Jewish civil year. For this reason its celebration was great among the people. The celebration began with the priests blowing the trumpets to announce the beginning of the religious celebration, and it was forbidden to the people to do any work on it, for this day became a holy convocation to which the law of the Sabbath and its rest applied fully (Lev 23:23). God commanded this feast for many reasons, the most important of which are:

29.0.1.en: 1- It is a preparation for the great feasts of the seventh month, which are the feast of Atonement and the feast of Tabernacles.

29.0.2.en: 2- The beginning of the season of agriculture.

29.0.3.en: 3- The trumpets recall God's promises to His people.

29.1.0.en: These verses mention the sacrifices offered at the feast. Taken as a whole, they are almost similar to the sacrifices of the previous feasts mentioned in (ch. 28..), and they can be summarized as follows:

29.1.1.en: 1- The day begins with the daily morning sacrifice, which is the burnt offering, and ends also with the evening burnt offering, and these are the two continual burnt offerings.

29.1.2.en: 2- The burnt offerings of the feast are offered, consisting of a bull, a ram and seven lambs one year old.

29.1.3.en: 3- The burnt offerings are accompanied by the usual offerings of flour mingled with oil and a drink offering in the same proportions as before.

29.1.4.en: 4- A he-goat is offered as a sin offering to make atonement for the sins of the people.

29.1.5.en: 5- A burnt offering is also offered on the occasion of the beginning of the month, apart from the burnt offering of the feast.

29.1.6.en: 6- Another sin offering particular to the beginning of the month is offered, consisting of another he-goat apart from the sin offering of the feast.

29.1.7.en: Remember God's promises to you every day, so that your heart may be at peace whatever problems you meet or fears war against you in the future, for your God loves you and never leaves you.

29.2.0.en: Nine days after the feast of trumpets, on the tenth day, comes the feast of Atonement, which was known for fasting, prayer and contrition ("ye shall afflict your souls"). For this reason one of the names of this feast was also "the feast of Forgiveness". Like the other feasts, the people were forbidden on it to do any work, in order to be free for worship and fasting. This feast was explained in detail in (Lev 16, 23) with all its ceremonies and steps, and here God again reminds the people of the importance of the spiritual meaning of this feast and affirms the meaning of forgiveness through blood. This feast carries in the substance of its rites the idea of redemption (see the explanation of Leviticus 16).

29.3.0.en: Like the preceding ones, these verses describe what was required to be offered of burnt offerings particular to this feast and the offerings accompanying them, besides the continual morning and evening burnt offerings.

29.3.1.en: Contemplate the love of Christ in His redeeming you on the Cross, so that you feel His surpassing love, and your heart rejoices, and on the other hand you refuse every sin, because it is the cause of His sufferings and His death on the Cross.

29.4.s.en: (3) The feast of Tabernacles and the freewill offerings

29.4.0.en: This feast was also mentioned in detail in (Lev 23:33-36), and here we review some of its meanings:

29.4.1.en: 1- The first spiritual meaning of this feast is that Israel, after entering and dwelling in the land, should remember the days of their earlier sojourn in the wilderness and God's provision for them, and also that the idea of man's being a stranger to the whole earth, and that he has another homeland, which is heaven, might be made firm.

29.4.2.en: 2- The period of the celebration was seven days, which they spent away from their houses and around the house of the Lord, in booths made of palm branches.

29.4.3.en: 3- This feast had another name, the feast of Ingathering and Thanksgiving, since it came after the people had finished gathering all the crops and the fruit of the trees.

29.4.4.en: 4- The first day of the feast, that is, the fifteenth of the seventh month, and the eighth day, that is, the twenty-second day, or the end of the feast, were holy religious convocations on which the people did no work.

29.5.0.en: In these verses God specifies the offering of each day separately during the seven days of the feast.

29.5.1.en: The offerings of all the days, in their general structure, are like the rest of the offerings and sacrifices of the feasts, but in the feast of Tabernacles there was one difference: the offering of the first day was thirteen bulls of the burnt offering, and every day God reduced it by one bull, until, when the seventh day came, the number of bulls was seven. With every daily offering God affirmed the continuation of offering the continual daily sacrifices, morning and evening, and this is of course besides the offerings of flour mingled with oil and the drink offering of wine.

29.5.2.en: We note here that the total of the sacrifices offered during the seven days of the feast amounted to the following: 70 bulls, fourteen rams, ninety-eight lambs, and seven he-goats.

29.5.3.en: The purpose of all this was that God might teach His people the virtue of thanksgiving at the end of the agricultural season, and that, just as God helped them and blessed them in everything, they too should give generously and not grudgingly.

29.5.4.en: The reduction in the number of bulls, one bull each day, signifies:

29.5.5.en: 1- God's commandments, which seem hard at first, but with time a person grows used to them and delights in them.

29.5.6.en: 2- The commandments of the Law gradually dwindle, and the need for Christ the Redeemer appears in the fullness of time.

29.5.7.en: My brother and my friend .. perhaps this subject touches us too, so let us ask ourselves a question .. Do we give to God generously, and do we give with joy, expressing to Him our thanks .. When your children succeed, or you succeed, do you remember to bring God an offering of thanksgiving by which you express your love for God!!?!

29.6.0.en: The eighth day was called the great day, and it points symbolically to eternity and its hoped-for rest. God asked them on this day to make it a day of retreat ("seclusion") for worship and praise, and to do no work on it (Lev 23:3, 23:36).

29.7.0.en: As for the burnt offerings and offerings of the eighth day, they were like the offering of any feast, consisting of a bull, a ram and seven lambs, and a sin offering is added to the burnt offerings, consisting of one he-goat, with all that accompanies that of offering and drink offering as usual.

29.8.0.en: These things ye shall do unto the Lord: that is, all that has been required of you to offer.

29.8.1.en: In your set feasts: that is, in the three preceding feasts which the seventh month of the religious year included.

29.8.2.en: The vow: the offering that a person pledges to God, which he must fulfill whatever the circumstances. The freewill offering: an optional offering not tied to a specific petition like the vow, but if it is lost before it is offered to God, God does not require the person to replace it.

29.8.3.en: At the end of the Lord's speech with Moses He emphasizes to him the necessity of offering all the preceding sacrifices for the feasts and seasons of the seventh month, and this ordinance does not cancel what people were accustomed to offer of vows and of other optional and additional offerings, such as the sacrifices and offerings of thanksgiving and peace, or any vows that a person pledges to God.

29.8.4.en: The communal worship that the Church offers is very like the offerings of the seasons that God appointed, but this does not cancel your own spiritual rule in your chamber, of prayers, readings and the like, for it is like the private offerings that God also asks of you.

29.9.0.en: As God spoke with Moses, so also the faithful servant told his people all that God had said to him. The following appears from these sacrifices:

29.9.1.en: 1- The necessity of the shedding of blood to obtain salvation: "without shedding of blood is no remission" (Heb 9:22).

29.9.2.en: 2- The sacrifice of the Cross has very many results and effects, which are made clear by these many kinds of sacrifices that signify it, for the sacrifice of Christ carries all the meanings found in the different Jewish sacrifices. Vows, an introduction: vows were discussed before in other places such as (Lev 7, 22, Num 6:2), but the focus here is on the obligation to keep them, and on some kinds of vows that require the consent of the husband or father, as we shall see.

30.0.s.en: (1) First: the vow of a man

30.0.0.en: We understand from the text that in an earlier conversation between God and Moses, Moses was told by God what the law of vows should be and how far a person is bound by them. Accordingly Moses gathered the heads of the people and the representatives of its tribes to tell them what God had commanded.

30.0.1.en: It is noted that a vow is one of these things:

30.0.2.en: 1- A certain act 2- An offering 3- Abstaining from something such as food.

30.0.3.en: The following is required of vows:

30.0.4.en: 1- That they be within the limits of God's commandments and not conflict with them, for Jephthah's offering of his daughter was a wrong vow (Judg 11:31).

30.0.5.en: 2- That they be within the limits of a person's capacity and means.

30.0.6.en: 3- That the vow be specific so that it can be fulfilled; one should not say "I offer the love of God", but "I offer such-and-such a thing".

30.0.7.en: 4- A person does not vow on behalf of another, as in a father's vow on behalf of his son or his wife.

30.0.8.en: 5- Whoever does not fulfill his vow is not punished by the priests and judges, but he is in the wrong toward the Lord and God is angry with him.

30.0.9.en: 6- A girl asks her father's permission, or a wife her husband's, when she vows.

30.0.10.en: 7- Not postponing the fulfillment of the vow, because in that is ingratitude toward God, and it exposes a person to forgetting the vow and not fulfilling it.

30.0.11.en: 8- It is preferable to write down the vow and keep the writing in a known place, to avoid forgetting it.

30.1.0.en: A bond: that is, the matter he has pronounced and is bound by, which is the subject of the vow.

30.1.1.en: The man, unlike the woman, who depended wholly on her husband or father for her support, and because the man is the source of income, there is nothing to nullify what he has pronounced with his mouth. Rather, if he vows and pledges an offering to God, he must keep it fully and fulfill it, and there is no one who can lift it from him or excuse him from it (Eccl 5:2-5).

30.2.s.en: (2) The vow of a girl before her marriage

30.2.0.en: These verses deal with two cases. The first is the case of the girl who has passed childhood and lives in her father's house, and the ruling on her vow is as follows: if she pronounces her vow and her father hears it and does not comment or object to what she said .. her vow becomes binding on her. But because her father has the right of guardianship over her and oversight of her upbringing, and is responsible for and manages all the material aspects, God gave him the right of refusal or objection. If he refuses or objects, the girl is as though she had vowed nothing, and God forgives her and requires nothing of her.

30.3.0.en: The second case is that of the same girl who was in her father's house and was under a previous vow she had not yet fulfilled, and who married and became another man's, not her father's. God gives her husband the same right that her father had, meaning that if he consents to the vow, with express consent or with consent by not objecting .. the vow she vowed in her father's house remains in force and binding ... But if he objects to her vow and prevents her from it, God does not require it of her but excuses her from it.

30.3.1.en: It is good for the girl to submit to her parents and not rush after her own thoughts and feelings, but to pray and consult her parents in every important matter. Better still, let there be a friendly relationship and understanding within the family, cared for by all parties, so that we secure a psychological stability that helps the growth of the spiritual life.

30.4.s.en: (3) The vow of the widow, the divorced woman and the married woman

30.4.0.en: The third case for a woman is that she is divorced or a widow. This is the case of a free woman who is not under the authority of a man or of anyone who has jurisdiction over her, so in everything she has pronounced and vowed she is bound to fulfill it.

30.5.0.en: The fourth and last case in the vow of a woman is that of the wife who made a binding vow while in her husband's house. The same preceding rule applies to her as regards the necessity of the husband's consent. But if the husband objects to the vow on the day he hears of it, this vow is void, and God does not require it of her.

30.6.0.en: These two verses are a review of what came in (vv. 10-12), the gist of which is the necessity of the husband's consent to his wife's vow, and in the case of his silence and not objecting, the vow remains in force and the woman is not excused from it.

30.7.0.en: Finally God gives a warning to the man that if he postpones his objection, on hearing the vow, to a later time, and then wants afterward to object, he has become the guilty one and the transgressor of God's commandment, and God considers him the breaker of the vow and not his wife: "he shall bear her iniquity".

30.8.0.en: At the end of the chapter comes this verse, making clear the purpose of the whole chapter, which is:

30.8.1.en: First: the duty of fulfilling vows, on the one hand.

30.8.2.en: Second: the conditions for carrying out the vow, and the relation of that to the girl's father if she is still in his house, or to her husband when she moves to his house.

30.8.3.en: How beautiful it is to offer love to God, but what matters is to follow up what I pronounce, that I may keep it and enjoy offering the love of God and receive His blessings.

31.0.0.en: Here God charges "Moses" with his last task before his death and his departure from this world to his fathers who went before him, and we note here several things:

31.0.1.en: First: the Lord asks this of Moses when he is a hundred and twenty years old and his days have drawn very near. The spiritual meaning here is that spiritual striving knows no time to stop or rest, so a person must continue in service and giving until the last days of his life, as long as he is able. Second: this war was just, for it was a war on a kingdom of evil and not on a particular people, since the Midianites were those who united with the Moabites against the people of God and put a stumbling block before them (ch. 25), and the woman "Cozbi the daughter of Zur", whom Phinehas the priest killed, was also a Midianite.

31.0.2.en: Third: the third and important meaning is that before you possess your inheritance, you must fight for it. The Promised Land is a type of the Kingdom of Heaven, and the Midianites are the enemies of God and the kingdom of Satan, and the rule is that there is no inheritance without victory and no victory without fighting, and it is a spiritual fight of course.

31.1.0.en: Armed: prepared for war, bearing their weapons.

31.1.1.en: Moses spoke to his people what God had spoken with him, and as a commander planning a battle he began to prepare his men, "his army". He asked them to choose men from all the tribes, a thousand men from each tribe, able to fight and bear arms. The wisdom of Moses here was the participation of the whole people in the war, so that no tribe might boast over another, on the one hand; and from the spiritual standpoint the meaning is that spiritual fighting and striving belong to all, and no one is exempt from it.

31.2.0.en: The presence of God in the midst of His people during the war was important, for the war was the Lord's and at His command, and the victory also came through Him. So that the people might understand this beautiful spiritual meaning, and also so that their hearts might be at ease in the first war they would fight for the new land, Moses sent with the people Phinehas the priest, the son of Eleazar, and with him also holy instruments from the furnishings of the tabernacle, which most commentators believe to be "the ark of the covenant". "Phinehas" also took the silver trumpets mentioned in (ch. 10), which were used in war to encourage the people and at the same time to glorify God.

31.3.0.en: Arm yourselves against Midian: that is, make war on Midian.

31.3.1.en: The people advanced and began the war against the Midianites, and the Lord gave them victory, and they killed all the males, who represented the greatest evil if they remained. The expression "every male" teaches us not to leave any amount of evil, even a small one, in our minds, because it will grow and return to war against us (Map 8).

31.4.0.en: The kings of Midian: that is, the heads of the great clans of the Midianites, as we now say "the mayor of the village".

31.4.1.en: This verse mentions the names of the five kings that Midian had, who were also killed with all the men, "the males". It also mentions here the killing by the sword of Balaam, the wicked prophet, who cast the stumbling block before the children of Israel. Although he had returned to his city (ch. 24:25), most commentators took his presence here with the Midianites as evidence against him that he went back and allied himself with them against the people of God, so that he deserved what befell him.

31.5.0.en: After the end of the war, the men of Israel burned all the cities of the Midianites with all their houses, but they kept for themselves the women, the little children and all the animals, and returned with all they had obtained to the place where the rest of the people were settled, east of the Jordan, opposite Jericho, in the place called "the plains of Moab" (Map 6).

31.6.0.en: Before they reached the place where the people dwelt, "the camp", the news of their victory reached everyone, so Moses went out, and with him Eleazar the high priest, to receive the victorious men of war, as an expression of their joy at the victory on the one hand, and as a kind of honor on the other.

31.6.1.en: Be careful to destroy evil and everything connected with it, so that the devil may not use it to make you fall again, and be confident that however great the power of sin, God is able to give you victory over it.

31.7.s.en: (2) The anger of Moses and his decisions

31.7.0.en: The officers of the host: that is, the commanders of the army, who were chosen from the leaders of the tribes, that is, the captains of thousands and captains of hundreds.

31.7.1.en: When Moses saw his victorious army coming, and with it Midianite women after all the men had been killed, his anger grew fierce and he was jealous with a holy jealousy for the Lord, for he saw with the eye of a spiritual leader what the ordinary person did not see. He cried out to his commanders, displeased and reproachful, asking how they had brought the women of the Midianites with them. He began to explain to them the reason for his refusal of what they had brought, which was that these women had been the cause of the people's falling into fornication earlier when they mingled with them, and because of them they worshiped the pagan god "Baal-peor", so the vengeance of God on the people was the plague that destroyed twenty-four thousand ... There also appeared in the words of Moses a reference to Balaam, who was behind this wicked counsel which he gave to "Balak" and the kings of the Midianites (ch. 25).

31.7.2.en: Moses was truly a servant and a leader, for he had foresight beyond the rest of the army commanders, and saw well the danger that threatened his people through keeping the women alive. The joys of victory and the multitude of captives did not distract him from this danger, so he did not flatter but rebuked these commanders.

31.7.3.en: My beloved brother ... your spiritual father is the person who has been entrusted by God with the salvation of your soul, and God has granted him to see the evil surrounding you, so listen to him and obey his directions, and in this you receive the blessing of obedience and escape from evil.

31.8.0.en: Moses firmly commanded the commanders of his army to kill all the male children, who, if they grew up, would become men resisting the people and might be affected by what happened to their fathers, and likewise all the women who were not virgins and who had defiled one another by seducing the children of Israel earlier, besides that they would carry a feeling of vengeance for the killing of their husbands, fathers and sons. As for the female children and the virgin girls, Moses spared them as captives and gifts for the men of his people. It is known that the women taken captive became Jewish and joined the people, and with time men married them, and such a woman was considered a wife and not a slave.

31.9.0.en: Moses continued in his speech, not forgetting all that God had commanded earlier in the laws of purification. He commanded the men to go outside the camp for seven days and to carry out the law of purification on the third and the seventh day as the Lord commanded (Lev 19:26, ch. 5:1-4, 19:11-13). Purification included not only the one who killed or touched a dead body .. but the captives, the virgin women, were also purified, because they would become Jewish and so must be subject to the Law; and likewise every garment and every movable thing they had brought with them, whether wood or wool, because it was defiled by the touch of the pagans, or by their own touch, that is, the children of Israel, after they had been defiled by touching the slain. The meaning includes everything else.

31.10.s.en: (3) The speech of Eleazar the priest

31.10.0.en: After Moses had finished his speech about the duty of purification, he left the speaking to Eleazar the priest, because by his priesthood he is responsible for applying the laws of the Lord, so he began to speak with the heads of the people, explaining to them how this purification was to be done.

31.11.0.en: Eleazar divided the spoil that had been taken into two groups. The first was the metals, and their purification was by putting them in the fire without melting them, or more precisely passing them through the fire, and after that the water of purification, which was spoken of before (ch. 19), is sprinkled on these metals. As for other things, such as leather, wood or cloth, which burn in fire, their purification is by sprinkling water on them only.

31.12.0.en: At the end of the time of purification, that is, the full week, the men wash their clothes and so complete their purification after their bathing too, and by this they are qualified to enter the camp and have fellowship with the people again.

31.12.1.en: Sin defiles us all, and repentance cleanses us from it, and the absolution that my father reads for me in confession restores me once again to fellowship with the Body of Christ .. So do not be slack and do not postpone .. but come forward and enjoy the purification and washing of your spirit.

31.13.0.en: After the men of war had completed their purification, and likewise the captives, God commanded Moses to count all the captives, the remaining virgins, as well as the living cattle and the goods. God associated with him in this work Eleazar the priest and the heads of the tribes, so that God might remove every suspicion from Moses, and also to teach us the necessity of collective work, of involving others, and of not holding authority alone.

31.13.1.en: The purpose of the counting was justice in dividing the spoil, to give a share to the fighters and also a share to those who did not take part in the war.

31.14.0.en: God commanded Moses to divide the spoil into two halves after the counting. The first half would be for the men of war who risked themselves for the people and exposed themselves to death, and the other half of the spoil would go to the whole people, because whoever did not go out to war was of unsuitable age, and so guarded the country and the houses of the fighters. Of course this carried justice on the one hand, and an incentive for the rest of the men to go out to war on the other.

31.14.1.en: Apart from the war of the children of Israel and the material spoil, the spiritual meaning here is that there is no heavenly reward except for the one who has conquered, and victory requires striving and fighting ... So be strong, my brother, and let no one take your crown.

31.15.0.en: Tribute: a necessary offering to God.

31.15.1.en: The command came here to the men of war to offer an offering from their half, and this offering is reckoned at one out of five hundred of the captives and of the beasts and the flocks. This tribute gives a portion to the priests, whom Eleazar represents, and God considered this offering as presented to Himself, "a heave offering of the Lord", because it is presented to His priests.

31.16.0.en: God did not forget the Levites either, so He commanded that a tribute also be taken from the other half of the spoil, which was given to the people, but the proportion would be one out of every fifty and not five hundred, because of course the number of the Levites is greater than the number of the priests. God also mentions here the necessity of honoring them and their obtaining a portion, since they are His servants and the keepers of the rites of His worship in His house.

31.17.0.en: And as the Lord commanded and ordered Moses, Moses the prophet and Eleazar did exactly as the Lord commanded.

31.18.0.en: In these coming verses is an explanatory detail of all that has been said before, and they are also considered a record in which the people wrote down the total of the spoil and the care taken to divide it exactly into two parts, and how from the first part came the share of the priests in the proportion God had set, and likewise from the second part, assigned to the people, came the share of the Levites in the proportion appointed for them. It is clear from these verses how abundant was the spoil the people obtained from this war, and the great blessing of God.

31.18.1.en: The idea of recording God's works and gifts is a spiritual idea practiced by many of the saints. For a person in times of distress may become prey to the enemy of good, who makes him doubt God's earlier works in his life; so what Moses and the people did here, in recording the numbers of the spoil and how it was distributed, is a testimony the people put on record against themselves, by their confession of God's wonderful work with them .. Would that we all did this, and remembered and recorded in our hearts and minds all that God has done with us. Indeed, some of us already write them down in their private meditations with God.

31.19.s.en: (5) The freewill offering of the leaders

31.19.0.en: Verses (48-52) carry a wonderful scene, worthy of note, comment and contemplation. The captains of thousands and the captains of hundreds, and with them the commanders of the divisions of the army, that is, the officers, came forward to Moses to speak with him, of their own accord.

31.20.0.en: The beginning of this speech by the commanders and leaders was an acknowledgment of a tangible fact, namely their recognition of God's great work with them in this war, for they returned from it without a single man being lost, which is unusual and unheard of in any war. The inspired text records for us how humble these leaders were, for they spoke to Moses at the start of their speech saying "thy servants".

31.21.0.en: Ankle chains: anklets, which are worn on the lower leg of a woman above her foot.

31.21.2.en: Bracelets: the necklace, or what is worn around the neck.

31.21.3.en: The subject of the speech was an offering of thanksgiving, consisting of the share of each one of them from the spoil of wrought gold, that is, worked gold, which they obtained from the adornment of the women, and they considered that this offering lifted up to God was an offering of atonement for their sins. The word atonement here also carries the meaning of "redemption" for them, and an acknowledgment that God redeemed them from death in this war.

31.22.0.en: Moses and Eleazar with him accepted this offering from them, since this offering was presented to God and the priest is God's steward, and consequently Eleazar is the one who received it. As for the amount of gold that was offered, it was very abundant, for by present weights its value was about two hundred kilograms of gold. This also shows how rich the people of the Midianites were, on the one hand, and the abundance of the shares which the leaders obtained, and consequently all the people.

31.23.0.en: Moses and Eleazar took the gold presented by the leaders and officers and brought it to the tabernacle and put it there, that is, presented it to the Lord, as a memorial for the children of Israel, meaning remembering the wonderful work of God in this victory, and that He is the only true God among the gods of the pagan nations and is able to crush His enemies. The word "memorial" before the Lord carries another meaning, which is that this offering was limited to the leaders only.

31.23.1.en: What the leaders of the people and its officers did is a beautiful and wonderful deed, expressing gratitude and how generous and kind their souls were, for they refused what was their right and offered it to God as a sacrifice of thanksgiving. This teaches us that it is fitting to offer to God from our surplus gains a sacrifice of thanksgiving which is more than the tithes, even by a little. If you cannot offer all that you have, will you offer some of it?

31.23.2.en: The tribes of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh
